items.title: Damon Wayans To Guest Star On NBC’s ‘St. Denis Medical’ Season 3 Premiere In ‘In Living Color’ Reunion; First-Look Photo
items.summary:
Damon Wayans will guest star on the Season 3 premiere of NBC's St. Denis Medical, reuniting him with David Alan Grier, his castmate from the sketch series In Living Color. Wayans plays Dr. Highland, described as a charming but pompous new physician who arrives at the underfunded Oregon hospital. Deadline reported the casting alongside a first-look photo from the episode.

The character is brought in to cover for Grier's Dr. Ron Kutcher while he recovers from surgery, and the premise leans on the reunion: patients and staff alike are taken with Highland and his pronouncements, with the exception of Alex. That gives Wayans and Grier a comic contrast to play without requiring the show to acknowledge the shared history.

Created by Justin Spitzer and Eric Ledgin, St. Denis Medical follows doctors and nurses trying to treat patients and stay sane at a hospital with too little money and too few people. The ensemble includes Wendi McLendon-Covey as administrator Joyce, along with Allison Tolman, Josh Lawson, Kahyun Kim, Mekki Leeper and Kaliko Kauahi.

Season 2 followed Joyce taking on more than she could manage after a large private donation, while the staff dealt with shortages, office friction and their own lives. Season 3 shifts toward romantic entanglements and personal struggles in the Emergency Department, pressures that push some employees close to breaking.

Ledgin is showrunner and an executive producer, with Spitzer, Simon Heuer, Bridget Kyle and Vicky Luu also executive producing. Universal Television is the studio, and the series is produced by More Bees, Inc. and Spitzer Holding Company.

Season 3 premieres Monday, November 2 at 8 p.m. on NBC. The first two seasons are streaming on Peacock.

items.title: Mariska Hargitay’s Best ‘Law & Order: SVU’ Episodes To Re-Air On NBC
items.summary:
NBC is setting aside a night of programming for Mariska Hargitay, airing a Law & Order: Special Victims Unit marathon built around three of her most acclaimed episodes as she prepares to host the Emmy Awards. The block runs Thursday, Sept. 10, according to Deadline, and doubles as a lead-in to her first turn as Emmys host.

The lineup is drawn from the show's awards history: "Charisma," an Emmy-nominated episode that first aired Nov. 16, 2004, at 8 p.m.; "911," the Emmy-winning episode from Oct. 4, 2005, at 9 p.m.; and "Undercover," nominated after its April 15, 2008 premiere, at 10 p.m.

Hargitay won Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series in 2006 for playing Olivia Benson and has been nominated eight times for the role. This year she is also nominated twice for My Mom Jayne, her documentary about her mother Jayne Mansfield, in Outstanding Documentary or Non-Fiction Special and Outstanding Director for a Documentary/Non-Fiction Program. She takes the Emmys stage at the Peacock Theater in downtown Los Angeles on Monday, Sept. 14 at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT.

The series itself continues alongside the tribute, with the Season 28 premiere set for Thursday, Oct. 8 at 9 p.m. ET/PT. Hargitay stars with Ice-T as Sgt. Odafin "Fin" Tutuola, joined by Kelli Giddish, Peter Scanavino, Kevin Kane and Aimé Donna Kelly. Later this year the show will pass 600 episodes.

SVU is executive produced by Dick Wolf, Michele Fazekas, Hargitay, Ken Brown, Rebecca McGill, Anastasia Puglisi and Peter Jankowski, with Universal Television producing in association with Wolf Entertainment.

items.title: Outside Lands 2026 Photo Gallery: The Strokes, Turnstile, Geese, Lucy Dacus, and More
items.summary:
Outside Lands 2026 has wrapped, closing out another edition of the festival in San Francisco's Golden Gate Park. The Strokes, Turnstile, Geese and Lucy Dacus were among the acts on the bill this year.

Consequence published a photo gallery from the weekend shot by veteran concert photographer Raymond Ahner, who covered the performances on site.

The images document the festival's headliners and supporting acts across the grounds. Golden Gate Park remains the event's home base, as it has been since the festival's start.

items.title: Fuerza Regida Announces New “This Is Our Dream” US Tour Dates
items.summary:
Fuerza Regida have added a second leg to their 2026 This Is Our Dream Tour, announcing ten new US dates for the fall. The Música Mexicana group will play amphitheaters and arenas across October and November.

The run opens October 3rd at Credit Union 1 Amphitheatre in Tinley Park, Illinois, and moves through Charlotte, Atlanta, Birmingham, Albuquerque, Wheatland, Bakersfield, Fresno and West Valley City before closing November 2nd at Red Rocks Amphitheatre in Morrison, Colorado.

Ticketing rolls out in stages, according to Consequence. A Verizon pre-sale starts Tuesday, August 11th at 10 a.m. local time, followed by a Spotify and Citi cardmember pre-sale at noon local time that day, and an artist pre-sale Wednesday, August 12th at 10 a.m. local time. General on-sale is Friday, August 14th at 10 a.m. local time via Ticketmaster.

VIP packages will be offered on select dates through vipnation.com, bundling premium tickets, a group photo with select members of the band, VIP lounge access and gift items.

The fall dates follow a sold-out stadium run earlier this year that included Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles and Citi Field in New York. The tour supports 111XPANTIA, which was nominated for Best Regional Mexican Music Album at the Grammys; the group's most recent single is "67."

items.title: Jerry Katzman, Former William Morris President, Dies at 89
items.summary:
Jerry Katzman, who helped build the modern business of television packaging and served as president of William Morris in the 1990s, died Sunday at his home in Los Angeles. He was 89. A family spokesperson said the cause was Parkinson's disease, The Hollywood Reporter reported.

Katzman joined the agency in 1972, starting in business affairs and rising to head of worldwide television. In that role he assembled talent and key elements behind series including The Cosby Show, Roseanne, Murphy Brown, Murder, She Wrote and The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air. His client list included Burt Reynolds, Angela Lansbury and Shelley Long.

He was named agency president in 1991, became vice chairman in 1997 and left in 2002. Afterward he joined the faculty of the UCLA School of Theater, Film and Television's Producers Program and consulted for companies including Anonymous Content. He also served as president of the Hollywood Radio & Television Society.

Born in Los Angeles on April 21, 1937, Jerome Katzman was the son of producer Sam Katzman, whose credits included the Elvis Presley pictures Kissin' Cousins and Harum Scarum and the Roy Orbison vehicle The Fastest Guitar Alive, and actress Hortense Petra. He attended Hawthorne Elementary and Beverly Hills High School before UC Berkeley and UCLA Law School, practiced law briefly and worked with his father in film before turning to the agency business.

His family described him as "a fearless leader, firm and decisive in his actions, who faced challenging decisions with great thoughtfulness," noting friendships he kept from grade school through retirement. He is survived by Carol, his wife of 66 years, whom he met at UC Berkeley; children Jeff, Jon and Kari; grandchildren Jackie, William, Neil, Josh, Jenna, Roland and Audrey; and great-granddaughter Naomi Juliette.

The family has asked that donations in his memory go to the UCLA Parkinson's Center, attention Dr. Jeff Bronstein and Jessica Vrazilek, the Jewish Federation Los Angeles, or the Cedars-Sinai Board of Governors.
